name: North Fork Flathead
gaugeName: N F Flathead nr Columbia Falls
blurb: Wild & Scenic water along the Glacier boundary. Logjams, gravel bars, and Polebridge pie.

sections.notes: Launch at the downstream Polebridge access. Coal Creek is a side-channel landing; low water and wood may complicate the take-out. Scout before committing to the channel.

distanceEvidence.sourceName: Flathead Rivers Alliance / DREAM river access surveys (April 2026)
distanceEvidence.note: Approximate distance between the published access-survey river mile markers. Braids, water level and the landing used can change the paddled distance. Individual access surveys with coordinates and photographs are linked from the map markers.

putInAccess.operator: US Forest Service / Flathead National Forest
putInAccess.sourceName: Flathead Rivers Alliance / DREAM access survey (April 2026)
putInAccess.note: Published access survey gives coordinates, landing photographs and river mile 33.8. Coordinate precision is four decimal places, not a surveyed ramp edge. Use the downstream Polebridge access below the ranger-station bridge, reached from the signed road off North Fork Road. The upstream access is a separate facility.

takeOutAccess.operator: US Forest Service / Flathead National Forest
takeOutAccess.sourceName: Flathead Rivers Alliance / DREAM access survey (April 2026)
takeOutAccess.note: Published access survey gives coordinates, landing photographs and river mile 24.5. Coordinate precision is four decimal places, not a surveyed ramp edge. Access is on a side channel beside an island. Low water may require a different launch spot on the bar; wood can obstruct the channel. Reach the access from the Forest Service road just before Coal Creek bridge.

sections.notes: Coal Creek launches from a side channel; wood and low water can require lining or dragging boats. Big Creek is a developed access with a day-use fee.

sections.notes: Includes the lower canyon rapids and the Shelf/Ledge above Glacier Rim. Scout and use whitewater skills; this is not a casual tube float. Great Northern Flats is an earlier exit before the lower rapids; confirm its access separately.

notices.title: Lower canyon whitewater
notices.text: Published paddler accounts describe Class III rapids between roughly river miles 9 and 4, within this section. Difficulty and the Shelf/Ledge hazard vary with flow; an access map does not identify a safe channel.
notices.sourceName: Rocky Mountain Canoe Club, July 2024 firsthand North Fork trip report, pp. 4–6

takeOutAccess.note: Published access survey gives coordinates, landing photographs and river mile 3.8. Coordinate precision is four decimal places, not a surveyed ramp edge. Follow the steep access drive downhill from North Fork Road to the river. This is upstream of the North Fork/Middle Fork confluence and is distinct from Blankenship.

mapAuditNote: Reviewed 2026-10-27 against Flathead Rivers Alliance / DREAM published access surveys, linked by the river partnership’s trip-planning page. All four named access coordinates and landing descriptions are documented. Polebridge now explicitly uses the downstream access; no take-out bank or route geometry is inferred.
